$comment: delta_rules.json — ALL document-independent policy for estimate comparison.
THE GENERAL RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO ENFORCE: nothing here may name a claim,
a carrier, a vehicle, an RO, or a file. If a fix can only be expressed by
naming one of those it is not a fix, it is a patch, and it will not survive
Code contains mechanism; this file contains policy. To change behaviour for
every future comparison, edit this file — never the annotator.
THREE SECTIONS OF THE SOURCE SPEC ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because they
already exist elsewhere in this repo and a second copy would drift:
canonical_ops -> data/operationAliases.json is the operation vocabulary.
The spec renamed every key (OP_PRE_SCAN for
PRE_REPAIR_SCAN); opCodeAliases below records the rename
returns 'Workfile' against a CCC stacked label block,
which is the defect that gate was written to fix.
numeric prose -> ai/numericIntegrity.ts already implements R11.

roles.targetSelectionNote: Annotate the HIGHER-grand-total estimate; the lower estimate is the source of the stamped comparison values. Authoritative per SKILL.md §2 and the owner-approved production behavior. The previous value 'lower_grand_total' was stale, contradicted every code layer and the skill spec, and misled the Test 99 audit into flagging compliant target selection as a defect (D4).

$extractionComment: R19. A missing_operation finding is a claim about the OTHER document, so it
requires having read the other document. The first image-only comparison
recovered no line items; the matcher compared 250 subject lines against an
empty pool and every one came back 'not written on the comparison estimate'.
minParsedRowsForLineVerdicts mirrors the absolute floor in
assessComparisonExtraction — an absolute count, not a ratio, because every
ratio computed from the rows that parsed rises as extraction gets worse.
$totalsVocabularyComment: R22. The totals reader accepts any row carrying letters and a number, which
on an OCR'd supplement made spending categories out of the publisher's
copyright block: 'All Rights Reserved ($0.00, 18 hr @ $0.00/hr)' shipped as
an AMOUNT DELTA finding. Reject list rather than allow list — an allow list
silently drops a real category when a platform renames one, and a dropped
category breaks the reconciliation with no visible symptom.
$contentComment: R24 (the Test 99 review's 'R25' — that number was already taken by the
changelog rule). The coverage gate (R19) correctly stopped a run that could
not read the comparison from accusing it of anything; what it could not
do was stop that run from SHIPPING. Test 99 (RO 22132) delivered a report
with dashes in both totals cells, no comparison identity, no rates, no
gap and two findings that were not differences. An empty report is not a
deliverable. R24 is armed by run_mode — a bundle that reports its mode
has enough identity to be held to this floor; the fixture bundles that
speculativeFindingTypes: findings a detector emits from vocabulary alone
(the structural review, the P-page review) do not count toward the floor;
a run made only of those has found nothing.
$detectorsComment: F4. A speculative detector may not fire without anchor evidence. Test 99's
'Structural frame and measurement verification' anchored to a hood test-fit
and a cavity-wax line on a front hit with no structural labor on either
document. structuralEvidence is what a document prints when structural
work exists: a labor class of S or F on a row, or a section / operation
in the structural vocabulary. Matched case-insensitively against the
documents' own text — never against a finding's prose.
$redactionComment: F7 (open since Test 98 F5). The export redaction policy blacks out every
identifier the raster pass can find, which on RO 22132 covered the shop's
street, phone and fax, the writer's name, the insurer and the claim number
— the things a supplement is filed under — while leaving the plate in the
clear. scope = 'natural_person' redacts a natural person's identity only
(owner / insured / claimant name, contact details beside those labels,
the VIN tail). scope = 'full' is the prior behaviour: insurer, claim,
policy, every phone and address as well. One line, applies to both
deliverables of a run. NOTE: this reverses the earlier standing
instruction that insurance information is redacted on export; the
Test 98/99 reviews asked for the reversal explicitly.

match.note: CCC underlines its own *-rows; never use underline for match

$authorityTableComment: R26 (the Test 99 review's 'R26'). U7 regressed on RO 22132: the 'Retrieved
for this claim' table listed five tier-5 how-to articles two paragraphs
under 'No retrieved authority is attached to a specific finding above'.
A tier at or below tableRequiresAttachmentAboveTier (the industry-body
tier and above) may be listed on retrieval alone; anything below it is
listed ONLY when it is attached to a finding. The meta-title patterns
below reject advice ABOUT authorities at the tier classifier, so a
how-to never reaches the table at any tier.

$rejectMetaTitlesComment: A source may back a finding only if it EVIDENCES the subject, not if it
discusses the subject. 'Tips on Finding OEM Position Statements' and
'How Important Are OEM Position Statements?' are advice about the
existence of position statements; neither IS one. RO 22116 cited the
first of those 11 times as the authority for OEM findings.
Matched case-insensitively against the whole title.
